answer: The divers map every octopus den along the reef wall and check each month whether the den is occupied, entering the result in the survey book. A dune den claimed from a photograph fails the survey: at the ridge of the wall the den must hold the shells and stones the octopus itself arranged, and a photograph shows no arrangement at all. Forging a survey means diving the wall for a season, mapping two hundred dens and paying 18,700, while the shale map in the survey office is kept until the next monsoon, so a den whose occupancy was never checked is left blank.
